verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated Sep-2025] CBK 'Use of Bank Cards in Kosovo' (September 2025 edition, data at 31/12/2024): 21,548 card-accepting terminals = 635 ATMs + 20,913 POS. Of the 635 ATMs, 634 offer cash withdrawal, 377 accept cash deposit and only 53 support credit transfer. Verified against the prior edition (October 2024, data at 31/12/2023): fleet 583 ATMs, of which 326 deposit-capable and 49 credit-transfer-capable. Only 18 of 20,913 POS terminals offer a cash-withdrawal (cashback) function. This is regulator statistics, not a live trigger.

verified_signals.entity: Government of Kosovo / Assembly - Draft Law on Payment Services
verified_signals.signal: A new Draft Law on Payment Services was approved at the 8th meeting of the Government of the Republic of Kosovo by Decision No. 08/08 dated 03/04/2026 (255-page trilingual Albanian/English/Serbian text). Its Article 3 states it transposes EU Directive 2015/2366 (PSD2), Directive 2009/110/EC (e-money), Directive 2014/92/EU (payment accounts) and Regulation (EU) 2024/886 on INSTANT CREDIT TRANSFERS IN EURO. Concrete provisions relevant to self-service: (a) Art. 1.29 defines 'advanced customer authentication' as authentication using two or more independent elements from knowledge / possession / inherence, with elements that dynamically link the transaction to a specific amount and payee; (b) Art. 1.15 EXCLUDES from the law's scope 'cash withdrawal services offered by means of ATM by providers, acting on behalf of one or more card issuers, which are not a party to the framework contract with the customer', on condition that they provide no other payment services and that the customer is still given information on withdrawal charges - i.e. an independent (non-bank) ATM deployer can operate in Kosovo without a payment-institution authorisation; (c) Art. 59.2 requires that where currency conversion (DCC) is offered before a transaction is initiated at an ATM, at a point of sale or by the payee, the party offering it must disclose to the payer ALL charges and the exchange rate to be used. CONTEXT ADDED BY VERIFIER: this is a re-draft. On 09/01/2026 Kosovo's Constitutional Court struck down the Assembly's December-2024 approval of the previous Law on Payment Services (one of 12 laws voided on a PDK complaint), so this law has to go through the Assembly again.
verified_signals.source_name: Office of the Prime Minister of Kosovo - PROJEKTLIGJI PER SHERBIMET E PAGESAVE / Draft Law on Payment Services
verified_signals.implies: Compliance-driven refresh of the whole self-service and acquiring estate: strong/advanced customer authentication on cards and channels, DCC screen-flow changes on every ATM and POS in the country, and a legal route for independent non-bank ATM operators - a new customer class for Printec ATM-as-a-service and managed services. Because the previous version was voided, this is also the single legal gate on Kosovo's SEPA accession, which raises its political priority.
verified_signals.likelihood: High for eventual enactment (SEPA membership depends on it); Medium on timing - it has to clear the Assembly again after the Constitutional Court annulment
verified_signals.followup: Track Assembly adoption and then the CBK secondary regulations, which will carry the actual compliance dates for the SCA and ATM/DCC articles. Ask CBK whether it intends to license independent ATM deployers and on what timetable - that is the door to an ATM-as-a-service play in a market where no such operator exists today.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Downloaded the 1.6 MB PDF and extracted the full text. Verified verbatim: footnote 2 'Draft Law no on Payment Services, has been approved in the 08-th Meeting of the Government of the Republic of Kosovo, with the Decision No. 08/08, dated 03.04.2026'; page count '255' confirmed by the '/ 255' page footers; trilingual layout confirmed. Art. 3.4 transposition list confirmed including 'Regulation (EU) 2024/886 ... as regards instant credit transfers in euro'. Art. 1.15 ATM-deployer exclusion confirmed verbatim including the 'Nevertheless, the customer shall be provided with the information on any withdrawal charges' proviso. Art. 59.2 DCC-at-ATM disclosure confirmed verbatim. Art. 1.29 'Autentifikimi i avancuar i konsumatorit' two-or-more-elements definition confirmed. verified_signals.entity: Assembly of Kosovo / CBK - Law on Banks and SEPA accession
verified_signals.signal: MATERIALLY CORRECTED. Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks (adopted by the Assembly 05/12/2024, promulgated by Presidential Decree No. DL-16/2026 dated 20/01/2026) was published in Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo No. 2 of 27/01/2026 and, per its Article 150, entered into force 15 days after publication (i.e. ~11/02/2026). Article 1.2 states it is harmonised with Regulation 575/2013/EU (CRR), Directive 2013/36/EU (CRD) and Directive 2014/59/EU (BRRD). On SEPA: CBK told Radio Free Europe that the pre-application was completed on 14/10/2024 and updated on 20/12/2024, that the European Commission accepted the documentation, and that 'the final application can only be submitted after the laws enter into force'. CBK estimates SEPA membership would save Kosovo citizens and businesses about EUR 55 million a year. THE CORRECTION: the researcher framed the Law on Banks as clearing the SEPA blocker. It only clears ONE of three. On 09/01/2026 the Constitutional Court ruled that the Assembly's approval of the Law on Banks WAS constitutional, but struck down 12 other laws from the same December-2024 batch - including the Law on Payment Services. So the SEPA gate is now the Payment Services law (and the AML law), not the Law on Banks, and the final SEPA application had still not been filed as of the last verifiable statement.
verified_signals.source_name: Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo No. 2 - LIGJI NR. 08/L-304 PER BANKAT (primary); Radio Free Europe / Evropa e Lire, 'Kosova pret anetaresimin ne SEPA per te kursyer miliona euro', quoting CBK and the Constitutional Court (press)
verified_signals.implies: SEPA accession forces IBAN and ISO 20022 message alignment (ISO 20022 = the structured payment-message standard SEPA runs on), sanctions and AML screening on cross-border euro flows, and re-certification of payment rails across all ten Kosovo banks - Printec AML, transaction-monitoring and payment-hub scope. The EUR 55m/yr CBK savings estimate is the political forcing function. But the timing now hangs on the Assembly re-passing the Payment Services law, so this is a 2027 event more than a 2026 one.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium - direction of travel is certain, timing slipped by the Constitutional Court annulment
verified_signals.followup: Confirm with CBK whether the final SEPA application has now been filed with DG FISMA / the European Payments Council and what the expected decision date is. Get the Constitutional Court judgment of 09/01/2026 from gjk-ks.org for the definitive list of which laws survived. Watch for the Assembly re-vote on the Payment Services law as the real starting gun.

At a 12-unit-a-year run rate plus a 168-unit fleet to keep current, this is the single largest named self-service estate in the country.
